questions: How must the recovered post-blend split-inheritance correction be integrated across sequence-player, single-node, and direct playback paths, and which rendered retail invariant validates it?
What are the complete nested virtual-model remap record semantics in the transformed branch inside 0x10089c40?
Which model/material decode defect causes the observed rainbow cloth independently of skeletal pose?

field_probes.label: bone_cache_or_mask
field_probes.role: Enumerates users of the C_BaseAnimating field used by SetupBones and BuildTransformations while locating the returned bone-matrix buffer.

field_probes.label: setupbones_output_source
field_probes.role: Enumerates readers of the field copied into SetupBones' optional output array.

findings.fact: The local quaternion and position channel decoders do not read bone Flags & 0x2.
findings.evidence: 0x10089b20 calls 0x100889f0 and 0x10088ba0 for each selected bone; neither decoder reads flags@bone+0x88.
findings.consequence: The flag is a post-decode hierarchy/application rule, not an alternate RLE encoding.

findings.fact: C_BaseAnimating::SetupBones dispatches the standard pose builder through vtable +0x208 and BuildTransformations through vtable +0x1ec.
findings.evidence: 0x10091c17-0x10091c5e; C_BaseAnimating slots 0x101e3f04=0x10091650 and 0x101e3ee8=0x1008fd00.
findings.consequence: The decoded pose, hierarchy construction, and entity/root composition are all on the live render-pose path.

findings.fact: BuildTransformations gives Flags & 0x2 bones split inheritance: rotation is root/entity rotation times local rotation, while translation is parent bone-to-world times local position.
findings.evidence: 0x1008ffa2-0x100901b5; flag test at 0x1008ffc5, custom branch at 0x1008fff3.
findings.consequence: A normal glTF node hierarchy and any fixed per-key quaternion multiplier are not faithful representations.

findings.fact: The BuildTransformations stack contract is positions, quaternions, root/entity 3x4 transform, then selected-bone bit list.
findings.evidence: SetupBones pushes the four arguments at 0x10091c3d-0x10091c5e; BuildTransformations consumes them at stack +0x6f60 through +0x6f6c.
findings.consequence: The special-bone rotation frame is the same entity/root transform used for root bones.

findings.fact: C_BaseAnimating::SetupBones is __thiscall with five callee-cleaned dword stack arguments, and its first five prologue bytes are one complete instruction with no relative operand.
findings.evidence: All four exits at 0x10091a2d, 0x10091a50, 0x100920cc and 0x100921cc are RET 0x14; 0x100919c0 is b830270000 (MOV EAX,0x2730) ahead of the _chkstk call at 0x101d0f00, and no instruction in the function branches to 0x100919c0-0x100919c4.
findings.consequence: The callee independently confirms the five arguments engine.dll stages, and the target takes an inline detour on the same shared backend as build_transformations without prologue relocation risk.

findings.fact: C_BaseAnimating::SetupBones receives the IClientRenderable subobject as this and adjusts down four bytes to reach the C_BaseAnimating, so its this equals the entity value the draw stream stores.
findings.evidence: 0x100919d6 moves ECX into EDI and 0x100919ea computes LEA ESI,[EDI-0x4] before dispatching on ESI; one theatre capture records the SetupBones bracket entity equal to the DrawModel render-info entity on every draw that resolved a bracket.
findings.consequence: This is CAP1.3's +4 seen from the other end: the skeletal evaluators run on the C_BaseAnimating while the renderable interface, the draw field, and SetupBones all share the subobject address, so a pose build joins a draw at delta zero and an evaluation at delta four.

findings.fact: C_BaseAnimating::InternalDrawModel is __thiscall with two callee-cleaned dword stack arguments, and its first five prologue bytes are three complete instructions with no relative operand.
findings.evidence: All five exits at 0x10092983, 0x100929b4, 0x100929cc, 0x100932e9 and 0x1009335f are RET 0x8; 0x10092970 is 83ec7c5356 (SUB ESP,0x7c; PUSH EBX; PUSH ESI), and no instruction in the function branches to 0x10092970-0x10092974.
findings.consequence: The outer draw frame takes an inline detour on the same shared backend as resolve_virtual_model_pose, so a pose build and the StudioRender draw it feeds can be bracketed under one enclosing generation.

findings.fact: C_BaseAnimating::InternalDrawModel submits the client renderable through VEngineModel006 slot +0x8.
findings.evidence: client.dll 0x10092f18-0x10092f51; VEngineModel006 acquisition at 0x100cb5e7-0x100cb5f3.
findings.consequence: The downstream SetupBones callback and palette application continue in engine.dll and StudioRender.dll, tracked by the companion specifications.

findings.fact: Transition history converts a saved pose with delta = inverse(currentRenderTransform) * savedEntityTransform before blending.
findings.evidence: client.dll 0x10091487-0x1009159c; AngleMatrix 0x101094b0, inverse 0x10108450, concat 0x10108a50, and raw stack arguments.
findings.consequence: Root and Flags-0x2 rotations are moved from the saved entity frame into the current render frame; root translation is moved too.

findings.fact: The outer included-model remap optionally transforms position by a per-record 3x4 matrix but always copies quaternion verbatim.
findings.evidence: client.dll 0x100969fb-0x10096ae8; 0x3c-byte mapping records and TransformPoint 0x10107f80.
findings.consequence: A faithful virtual-model resolver must retain authored position-frame mappings without inventing a rotation retarget at this layer.

findings.fact: A client entity class writes one vtable per subobject, and the second subobject sits at this+0x4.
findings.evidence: 0x10002d8b through 0x10002dab store 0x101e3cfc at +0x0, 0x101e3ca4 at +0x4, 0x101e3c6c at +0x8, 0x101e3c30 at +0xc and 0x101e3c1c at +0x10; C_BaseEntity::C_BaseEntity at 0x1008f3c0 writes the same five displacements with its own vtables at 0x1022d6d4, 0x1022d67c, 0x1022d644, 0x1022d608 and 0x1022d5f4, and C_BaseEntity::~C_BaseEntity restores exactly those five.
findings.consequence: CAP1.3's +4 is a declared multiple-inheritance layout rather than a heap coincidence: the interface subobject the draw stream and SetupBones both name is the second base, four bytes into the object, and the constructors say so independently of any capture. One theatre capture measures the same +4 between the entity and renderable addresses the actor census records.

findings.fact: A vtable carrying BuildTransformations at +0x1ec belongs to one concrete class rather than to every skeletal entity, so it does not identify a shared construction path.
findings.evidence: 0x101e3cfc carries slot +0x1ec = 0x1008fd00 and slot +0x208 = 0x10091650, the two dispatch targets SetupBones pins, yet exactly one instruction references it as data (0x10002d8b) and its writer 0x10002d80 has exactly one caller (0x10002c40). A hook installed on 0x10002d80 for a 90-second theatre capture recorded zero constructions while four skeletal actors were posed.
findings.consequence: Each derived class carries its own vtable with the same inherited slots, so a construction target must be the shared base C_BaseEntity::C_BaseEntity rather than any class whose vtable happens to hold the pose slots.

findings.fact: C_BaseEntity::C_BaseEntity is 0x1008f3c0 and C_BaseEntity::~C_BaseEntity is 0x1008f5c0; both are __thiscall with no stack arguments and both are the shared base of the client entity hierarchy.
findings.evidence: The constructor is 53 55 56 57 8b f1 (PUSH EBX; PUSH EBP; PUSH ESI; PUSH EDI; MOV ESI,ECX) with 12 callers; the destructor is 53 56 57 8b f9 (PUSH EBX; PUSH ESI; PUSH EDI; MOV EDI,ECX) with 15 callers and one exit at 0x1008f6e5 that restores this into ECX and JMPs to 0x1009ddc0 rather than returning. Each prologue is complete instructions with no relative operand, nothing branches into either, and the two are the only references to the vtable 0x1022d6d4.
findings.consequence: Every client entity construction and destruction passes through this pair, so a lifetime record covers the whole hierarchy; restricting it to the skeletal actors CAP2.3 names is an offline join against the actor census rather than a live filter.

findings.fact: Every Flags & 0x2 bone in the patch-first character corpus uses the conventional hierarchy-FK inverse bind, not a split-inheritance inverse bind.
findings.evidence: pipeline/src/elysium_pipeline/validation/validate_skeletal_pipeline.py independently evaluates all 373 flagged bones across 433 character skeletons; worst boneToWorld * poseToBone identity error is 7.36e-6.
findings.consequence: Split inheritance belongs only to live pose construction; skin binding and generated inverse binds remain conventional.

findings.fact: The pose chain below resolve_virtual_model_pose shares one seven-dword __cdecl contract: (studiohdr, positions, quaternions, sequence, cycle, poseParameters, boneMask).
findings.evidence: 0x100968a0 is __thiscall ending RET 0x18 and forwards its six stack arguments plus the studiohdr it obtains from 0x1008f900(-1) to 0x10089c40 at 0x1009693a, cleaning with ADD ESP,0x1c. 0x10089c40 reaches its arguments at frame+0x27c8..0x27e0 after MOV EAX,0x27c4 / _chkstk and ends in a bare RET, and stages the same seven for 0x10089740 at 0x1008a046 with ADD ESP,0x1c.
findings.consequence: A capture hook at either frame reads the owner studiohdr as argument zero rather than inferring it, and the two frames take the same argument decoder.

findings.fact: decode_selected_bones is __cdecl (studiohdr, positions, quaternions, StudioAnimDesc, cycle, boneMask); its fourth argument is the animation descriptor of one blend cell.
findings.evidence: 0x10089b20 reads its arguments at frame+0x04..0x18 after SUB ESP,0x8 and four pushes, and ends in a bare RET; the single-cell call site 0x1008993d builds the fourth argument as studiohdr + LocalAnimIndex@268 + grid cell * 72 and cleans with ADD ESP,0x18. The callee reads numframes at +0xc and animindex at +0x30 of that pointer.
findings.consequence: Owner-local animation identity is witnessed per fired cell as a pointer into the owner image, so CAP2.5's file offset is that pointer minus the studiohdr and the index is (pointer - hdr - LocalAnimIndex) / 72.

findings.fact: Frame selection is floor((numframes - 1) * cycle), and the remainder is the interpolation fraction passed to both channel decoders.
findings.evidence: 0x10089b41-0x10089b5e loads numframes@+0xc of the animation descriptor, decrements it, multiplies by the cycle argument, calls __ftol, and passes both the integer and the difference to 0x100889f0 and 0x10088ba0.
findings.consequence: Clip duration divides by frames - 1, not frames, which settles the sampling-law question the evidence document lists as open.

findings.fact: The per-bone animation records inside a StudioAnimDesc have a fixed 32-byte stride, and the selected-bone mask is a dword array beginning four bytes into the mask argument.
findings.evidence: 0x10089b20 walks NumBones@240 advancing the bone by 0xa0, positions by 0xc, quaternions by 0x10 and the animation record by 0x20 per bone, and gates each bone on mask[4 + (i >> 5) * 4] & (1 << (i & 31)).
findings.consequence: The animation block is indexable without decoding preceding bones, and the +4 the capture probe already copies is the array itself rather than a guessed displacement.

findings.fact: StudioSeqDesc carries the blend axes at groupsize[2]@572, paramindex[2]@580, paramstart[2]@588 and paramend[2]@596, and its 16x16 animation grid at 56 has a 32-byte row stride.
findings.evidence: 0x10089500 indexes all four arrays as base + axis * 4 off the descriptor; 0x10089740 branches on groupsize[1] then groupsize[0] at 0x100898fd to select one, two or four cells, reading grid[i1][i0] at descriptor+0x38+(i1*16+i0)*2 and grid[i1+1][i0] at descriptor+0x58+(i1*16+i0)*2. Across the installed character tree all 294 multi-blend sequences satisfy groupsize[0] * groupsize[1] == numblends@52, with distribution 9x1 235, 3x3 49, 2x1 6 and 5x1 4.
findings.consequence: The grid is a groupsize[0] by groupsize[1] blend space rather than a raw 16x16 array, and a decoder that reads only cell [0][0] silently drops every one of those 294 sequences.

findings.fact: A pose parameter descriptor is 20 bytes at LocalPoseParamIndex@388 with name@0, flags@4, start@8, end@12 and loop@16; a sequence axis normalizes its parameter into [0,1] over paramstart..paramend and clamps.
findings.evidence: 0x10089500 reads hdr+0x184 + index * 0x14 and uses +0x10 as a wrap modulus when non-zero, then normalizes (value - start@8) / (end@12 - start@8) and remaps through the descriptor's paramstart and paramend before clamping to 0..1 and deriving the cell index against groupsize. The installed corpus reads move_yaw and hit_yaw with flags 1, start -180, end 180 and loop 360, matching the -180/180 paramstart/paramend of every 9x1 sequence that selects them.
findings.consequence: Pose parameter range, wrapping, normalization and blend mapping are established, so a reproduced evaluator no longer has to guess whether values are normalized before lookup.

findings.fact: StudioSeqDesc carries an autolayer count at 660 and an autolayer index at 664, and each entry is a four-byte sequence index the dispatcher evaluates recursively.
findings.evidence: 0x1008a06b reads descriptor+0x294 as a loop bound and 0x1008a079 reads descriptor+0x298 as the array base, advancing four bytes per iteration and passing each dword as the sequence argument to a recursive 0x10089c40 call followed by 0x10088e10.
findings.consequence: A sequence contribution can fire further sequence contributions inside one pose build, so contribution multiplicity is a property of the data rather than of the caller.

findings.fact: The virtual sequence index space is the last include group's sequence base plus its count, and an index below NumLocalSeq@272 resolves against the model's own sequences.
findings.evidence: 0x100968e5-0x10096917 computes the bound from the last of NumIncludeModels@404 groups at IncludeModelIndex@408 with stride 0x74, reading base at group+0x08 and count at group+0x0c, and falls back to NumLocalSeq when the model has no include models; 0x10089c5b takes the local path on the same comparison.
findings.consequence: A captured sequence index is only meaningful beside the studiohdr it was resolved against, which is why owner identity travels on every contribution record.

findings.fact: A runtime include-model group is 116 bytes carrying the loaded model at +0x04, its sequence base at +0x08, its sequence count at +0x0c, a bone remap array at +0x10 with 56-byte records, and a 24-entry pose parameter remap at +0x44.
findings.evidence: 0x10089c84-0x10089d1b walks the groups at stride 0x74, calls vtable slot +0x4 on the object at group+0x04 to obtain the included studiohdr, remaps 0x18 pose parameter slots through the shorts at group+0x44, and then walks group+0x10 records advancing 0x38 per target bone.
findings.consequence: Owner resolution and the shared-animation remap are both reachable from the group entry, and the 24-slot pose parameter remap bounds the parameter span a contribution record must retain.

findings.fact: The three contribution frames take a five-byte inline detour without prologue relocation: 0x10089740 is a0c9024910, 0x10089c40 is b8c4270000, and 0x10089b20 is 83ec085355.
findings.evidence: Read from the pinned client.dll at file offsets for those RVAs; 0x10089740 is one MOV AL,moffs32 with an absolute operand, 0x10089c40 is one MOV EAX,imm32, and 0x10089b20 is SUB ESP,0x8 with two pushes. No branch inside any of the three targets a byte in its first five. The same extraction reproduces the already-installed setup_bones signature b830270000.
findings.consequence: All three take the shared inline backend on the same terms as the existing targets; 0x10089500 begins 83ec08538b5c241c and needs the instruction-aware relocation the backend already performs.

functions.label: dispatch_model_pose
functions.role: Resolves a virtual sequence index to its owning include model, remaps pose parameters and bones across the group boundary, reaches the sequence evaluator on the local path, and recurses over the descriptor's autolayers. The nested transformed remap branch remains open.

functions.label: evaluate_sequence_pose
functions.role: Resolves both blend axes through 0x10089500, selects one, two or four cells of the sequence descriptor's 16x16 animation grid on the two group sizes, and calls the per-bone animation loop once per cell.

functions.label: resolve_blend_axis_weight
functions.role: Maps one pose parameter onto one blend axis of a sequence descriptor, wrapping and normalizing it against the parameter descriptor and the axis range, and returning the cell index and the fractional weight evaluate_sequence_pose blends with. Four callers: two per evaluation from 0x10089740 and two from 0x1008c060.

functions.label: decode_selected_bones
functions.role: Walks selected bones and decodes quaternion and position channels.

functions.label: decode_bone_quaternion
functions.role: Decodes four quaternion RLE channels, falls back to bind components, and interpolates frames.

functions.label: decode_bone_position
functions.role: Decodes three position RLE channels relative to bind position.

functions.label: resolve_virtual_model_pose
functions.role: Selects the base or included studio model and maps its pose into target arrays.

functions.label: transform_point_3x4
functions.role: Applies a 3x4 affine matrix to a position; used by transformed virtual-model mapping records.

functions.label: invert_rigid_3x4
functions.role: Inverts an orthonormal 3x4 entity transform for transition-history frame conversion.

functions.label: matrix_get_column
functions.role: Extracts a 3-vector matrix column; transition history uses column three to update a root position.

functions.label: angle_position_matrix
functions.role: Builds a 3x4 transform from Source angles and position for saved/current entity frames.

functions.label: maintain_sequence_transitions
functions.role: Maintains 0x4c-byte previous-sequence records, resolves their poses, moves root/Flags-0x2 orientation through saved/current entity frames, and blends them into the current pose.

functions.label: build_standard_pose
functions.role: Widely shared virtual pose builder: base sequence, transition history, autoplay sequences, virtual hook, then bone controllers.

functions.label: c_baseanimating_build_transformations
functions.role: C_BaseAnimating::BuildTransformations; builds bone-to-world matrices from local positions/quaternions and applies the Flags-0x2 split-inheritance rule.

functions.label: c_baseanimating_setupbones
functions.role: C_BaseAnimating::SetupBones entry point; manages cache/masks and dispatches pose construction plus model-space matrix construction through virtual slots.

functions.label: c_baseanimating_get_studio_hdr
functions.role: Resolves the entity's studiohdr_t from the model cache; called with -1 for the entity's own model. The capture probe calls it rather than hooking it, so the skeletal streams name the same header the draw stream reads.

functions.label: build_layered_pose
functions.role: Specialized pose builder: base sequence, transition history, weighted layers/overlays, virtual hook, then bone controllers.

functions.label: procedural_geometry_pose_consumer
functions.role: Large specialized consumer that samples poses while generating procedural geometry; it is not the base SetupBones hierarchy bridge.

functions.label: bone_cache_accessor
functions.role: Small reader of the C_BaseAnimating +0x6e8 field; inspect ownership and return semantics.

functions.label: bone_cache_consumer_a
functions.role: Consumes the +0x6e8 field after bone setup; candidate downstream matrix user.

functions.label: bone_cache_consumer_b
functions.role: Consumes the +0x6e8 field near SetupBones; candidate cache copy or render bridge.

functions.label: setupbones_direct_caller_a
functions.role: One of three direct client.dll callers of C_BaseAnimating::SetupBones; inspect for an override or downstream submission bridge.

functions.label: setupbones_direct_caller_b
functions.role: One of three direct client.dll callers of C_BaseAnimating::SetupBones; inspect for an override or downstream submission bridge.

functions.label: setupbones_direct_caller_c
functions.role: One of three direct client.dll callers of C_BaseAnimating::SetupBones; inspect for an override or downstream submission bridge.

functions.label: c_baseanimating_drawmodel
functions.role: C_BaseAnimating::DrawModel render entry; dispatches an internal drawing virtual after establishing render state.

functions.label: c_baseanimating_internal_drawmodel
functions.role: C_BaseAnimating main-vtable slot +0x1f4 reached from DrawModel; submits the renderable through VEngineModel006 slot +0x8.

functions.label: concrete_animating_construct
functions.role: Constructor of one concrete class derived from C_BaseAnimating; writes the vtable 0x101e3cfc whose slots the pose specification samples. It has one caller and a theatre capture hooked on it recorded no construction, so it is not the shared skeletal construction path.

functions.label: c_baseentity_construct
functions.role: C_BaseEntity::C_BaseEntity; writes the five C_BaseEntity subobject vtables at 0x1022d6d4 and has 12 callers, so every client entity's construction chain reaches it.

functions.label: c_baseentity_destruct
functions.role: C_BaseEntity::~C_BaseEntity; restores the same five subobject vtables at entry and tail-calls its base teardown, and has 15 callers, so every client entity destruction passes through it.
